title: Take the rotten vegetables out of a packed produce container and put them in the waste bin
instruction: Take the rotten vegetables out of the produce container and put them in the waste bin.
context: Clearing out the produce drawer or a crisper box is a routine household chore: a spoiled piece left among fresh ones spreads mold to its neighbours and spoils them too, and USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service advises discarding moldy soft produce (fsis.usda.gov, "Molds on Food"). The instruction already asks for the spoiled pieces to be removed. The difficulty is physical: each tomato is 8.6-8.8 cm across and the gripper opens 9.4 cm, and the tomatoes stand 1 cm from the peppers beside them.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Produce container: a Rubbermaid FreshWorks 3-gallon produce saver, clear plastic, 45.7 x 30.5 cm and 16.0 cm tall (18 x 12 x 6 5/16 in), lid and insert removed, walls about 3 mm, centred at (36.0, -3.0) with its long side along y, taped to the table. Waste bin: an OXO Good Grips Easy-Clean 1.75 gallon compost bin, charcoal plastic, 25.8 cm along x by 21.1 cm along y and 30.5 cm tall (10.15 x 8.3 x 12 in), lid open, centred at (40.0, -49.0), taped to the table. In the container, on its floor, centres at: rotten tomato A (29.5, -20.1); red bell pepper A (29.5, -9.6); rotten tomato B (29.5, 0.9); red bell pepper B (29.5, 11.4); zucchini (42.5, -14.7), its length along y. Each rotten tomato: a firm large red tomato prepared as in reset_notes, 8.8 x 8.6 x 5.9 cm, 220 g, stem end up, with a standardized dark patch 4.0 cm across on its upper shoulder beside the stem, turned so the patch faces the front of the table (towards the robots); about 1 cm clear of its neighbours along the row. Each red bell pepper (fresh produce): 8.5 x 10.2 x 10.2 cm, 170 g, stem up. Zucchini (fresh produce): 19.7 x 5.4 x 5.2 cm, 297 g, dark green. The rotten vegetables are the two tomatoes with the dark patch; the peppers and the zucchini are fresh. The left arm has nothing to do.
scoring: Tools: a phone camera, a ruler and the trial video. Before each trial, tape marks outline each good piece's starting place on the container floor. Fresh produce kept: both peppers and the zucchini lie inside the produce container's walls, each with its centre within 2 cm of its starting centre (ruler against the marks). In the bin: a tomato rests inside the bin's walls, below its rim. Released: both grippers are open and at least 7 cm from both tomatoes, and both tomatoes are still, held for 1 s in the video. At the end: 0 if any pepper or the zucchini is outside the container or more than 2 cm from its start, or no tomato is in the bin; 0.5 with one tomato in the bin; 0.75 with both in the bin but a gripper still within 7 cm of a tomato or a tomato still moving; 1.0 with both in the bin and released, held for 1 s.
reset_notes: The standardized dark patch is what marks a tomato as rotten, so every trial's tomatoes look alike. Preparing a pair takes under 10 minutes, including drying: choose two firm large tomatoes 8.5-9 cm across and 5.5-6.5 cm tall, 200-240 g on a kitchen scale, with no cracks or soft spots, and spares. Cut a 4.0 cm round hole in a piece of card. Hold the card against the upper shoulder of each tomato, with the hole's centre 2.5 cm from the stem scar, on the side that will face the robots, and dab black edible food-colouring gel through the hole with a foam dauber, twice, to an even opaque dark patch 4.0 cm across; lift the card straight off and let the patch dry 5 minutes until it is not tacky. Each trial use a pair with intact, dry patches, stem end up with the patch towards the robots, at the listed centres; stand the peppers and lay the zucchini back at theirs, checking the 1 cm gaps beside each tomato with a ruler and re-taping the outline marks. Handle the tomatoes by their sides so the patch is not rubbed, and repaint a patch or swap in a spare whenever one is smeared, chipped or the skin is split. Wipe the gripper pads, table and containers afterwards and empty the bin.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz. Each piece of produce is one rigid body with a convex-hull collider, with the size and mass of its 3D asset (marso SimReady, CC BY 4.0): the dark patch is a texture, as the real tomatoes' patch is paint on a firm tomato, and tomatoes do not squash or leak. The containers are fixed straight-walled boxes with 3 mm walls and floors (the real bin tapers; its lid is open and the produce container's lid and vented insert are removed).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the right arm went to the zucchini and pushed it about at the back of the container for the whole run, and never touched a tomato or the bin); demo: 1.0
